insights.summary: H2 FY26 revenue doubled to ₹103 Cr with a 26% EBITDA margin, taking FY26 to ₹153 Cr (+55%), a 22% EBITDA margin and ₹21 Cr PAT (14%), in line with or above guidance; working capital fell from 570 to 370 days after the IPO. Management guides ~40% annual growth for three to five years (FY27 excluding data centres), a 20-24% EBITDA margin, ₹1,000 Cr revenue in five years, and spares rising back to 15-20% of revenue; the order book is ₹270 Cr (1.8x revenue) with 64% share of naval HVAC. The new Hanbarwadi plant starts in June, and a first data-centre reference installation is targeted in FY27.

Working capital down to 370 days from 570

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: So, as a management of this company, we definitely are standing by our word.

analyst_questions.answer: FY27 less skewed, but shipyard delivery schedules still make H2 bigger.
Supplier advances and GST credit (18% input vs 5% output on warships); refund expected in H1.
~₹2,500 Cr naval HVAC over two years from ₹2.3-2.4 lakh Cr of approvals; ~₹500 Cr merchant marine.
Working capital from internal accruals and banks; balance sheet not leveraged.

red_flags.text: Working capital still ~370 days; receivables ~250 days.
Fixed-price contracts; unprecedented metal inflation will dent margins a little.
Lost some new-build tenders; growth relies on Navy ordering pace.
Half-yearly reporting only; numbers swing sharply between halves.

watch_next: H1 FY27 revenue (less H2-skewed than FY26)

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Naval AC plants, refrigeration plants, HVAC systems and control panels; marinised split ACs; test rooms and calorimeters
business_snapshot.customers: Indian Navy shipyards and retrofit programmes; merchant shipbuilders; data-centre operators via Smardt; Danfoss compressor users
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: equipment for new builds and retrofits ~93%, spares and service ~7%
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Navy growing from ~150 to ~230 ships, retrofits, merchant shipbuilding push, data-centre cooling
